docs.text: Frontend Developer, Co-op Intern at AiFinancial. Frontend co-op on a production React and TypeScript monorepo. I spent the term on the seam between the frontend and the backend contract, and left the codebase generating its API clients instead of hand-writing them.
Evaluated four approaches to API integration — Orval, Pact, Hey API and openapi-typescript — documented the trade-offs as ADR-0005, and presented the recommendation to other development teams.

Found inconsistencies between how the frontend called the API and what the backend REST contracts actually promised, then helped introduce Orval to generate TypeScript clients directly from the OpenAPI specification, so the mismatch could not silently return.
Migrated production React components from hand-written fetch patterns to generated TanStack Query hooks, cutting roughly 60% of the code in each component.
Built the Phase 1 prototype infrastructure — Orval code generation, an MSW mock server and the TanStack Query wiring — inside a pnpm monorepo authenticated with MSAL.
Wrote Vitest component tests against MSW handlers, and tracked down a token synchronisation defect between two ApiClient instances in the authentication flow.
Worked in a cross-functional Agile team with React/TypeScript frontend and Java/Spring Boot backend developers, through feature branches, rebases, pull requests, Docker and CI/CD.

docs.text: This Portfolio. A portfolio that runs its own NLP models in your browser. Next.js 16 front end with a Python training pipeline. Every intelligent feature on this site runs client-side: transformer embeddings for search, a language model trained on my own writing for next-word prediction, and a requirement-matching engine for job descriptions. No API keys, no per-request cost, no third-party model calls.
This Portfolio: Transformer sentence embeddings computed at build time in Python and re-computed for queries in-browser with ONNX Runtime Web, so search understands meaning rather than keywords
This Portfolio: A Kneser-Ney smoothed n-gram language model trained on my own writing, serialised to a compact trie and running entirely client-side
This Portfolio: A job-description matcher that extracts requirements, embeds each one, and maps them onto specific evidence from my work, including the gaps
This Portfolio: A UMAP projection of the project embeddings rendered as an interactive WebGL constellation, where distance is semantic distance
This Portfolio: A live systems page reporting real latency, model sizes and vector counts rather than a static architecture diagram

FlowTrace. Local-first visual problem mapping. A canvas tool for breaking a tangled problem into nodes and tracing the dependencies between them. Everything stays on your machine. No account, no sync, no server that can go down or read your work.
FlowTrace: Directed-graph canvas built on @xyflow/react with automatic dagre layout that preserves the user's mental map between relayouts
FlowTrace: Local-first persistence with no backend, no account and no network dependency
FlowTrace: Zustand state architecture tuned to keep large graphs interactive during drag
FlowTrace: Test suite of 60+ specs in Vitest covering graph mutations, layout and persistence

Work Plug. A marketplace for skilled trades. A two-sided platform where skilled workers publish a verifiable profile — trade, rate, availability, service area, past work — and clients search, filter and book them directly.
Work Plug: Two-sided marketplace with distinct worker and client models, search and multi-facet filtering by rate, rating, availability and location
Work Plug: Authentication with email confirmation flows and session handling
Work Plug: Booking model that keeps worker availability consistent under concurrent requests
Work Plug: Also the subject of a full PMBOK project-management study: stakeholder, quality, human resource and communications management plans, which I led as project manager

Student Outcome Networks. Neural networks predicting academic performance. Two neural networks over a student-records dataset: a regression model estimating final GPA, and a classifier identifying high academic achievers early enough for an intervention to matter.
Student Outcome Networks: GPA regression and high-achiever classification trained on the same normalised feature set
Student Outcome Networks: Early stopping with patience and model checkpointing, so the deployed weights are the best epoch rather than the last
Student Outcome Networks: Feature normalisation throughout, which is the difference between a sigmoid network that learns and one that stalls
Student Outcome Networks: Companion LSTM sequence model reaching 61.68% validation accuracy on synthetic code generation

Churn Prediction on AWS. Cloud machine learning pipeline. An end-to-end customer churn pipeline built and trained on AWS: ingestion, feature engineering, model selection and evaluation, with a Random Forest reaching 86.25% accuracy and 93.17% AUC.
Churn Prediction on AWS: Full pipeline on AWS from ingestion through evaluation
Churn Prediction on AWS: Random Forest at 86.25% accuracy and 93.17% AUC, with AUC treated as the meaningful metric on imbalanced data
Churn Prediction on AWS: Comparative model selection rather than fitting one estimator and reporting it

RARS. Automatic emergency alerting after a collision. A road-accident response system that detects a collision and automatically sends the location and situation to emergency services and to the driver's family, for the case where the driver cannot make the call themselves.
RARS: Collision detection with a cancellation window to suppress false positives before any alert is sent
RARS: Automatic dispatch of location and incident detail to emergency services and designated family contacts
RARS: Designed around the case where the user is unable to interact with the device at all

Incident Record. IT service management ticketing. A ticketing system for IT teams: log system failures, software bugs and network problems, assign them to technicians, and track resolution to keep downtime measurable.
Incident Record: Incident lifecycle with assignment, status transitions and resolution tracking

Incident Record: Full CRUD with validation at the API boundary rather than only in the form
